title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Aeronautical Chart. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Aeronautical Chart
options.lineage: Jeppesen enroute charts, instrument approach plates, FAA sectionals
options.thesis: Your life and work drawn as a navigator's chart: a real route over real coordinates, each case briefed as an approach plate.
options.viewport: Full-bleed chart of the whole route (NYC, Plano, San Jose, Atlanta, Richardson, Singapore) on a live graticule; name and intro sit in the chart's title panel; New York pulses as 'you are here'.
options.risk: Aviation jargon can bury the research; every chart device needs a plain-language label and the metaphor must stay notation, not costume.

raised.raise: Nothing glides: distance, heading and local-time readouts step in whole units with one overshoot, like a mechanical counter.
Everything is measured: every element snaps to the chart graticule and carries its reading; nothing floats off-grid.
Your route is inked, the rest is planned: legs and cases you have visited turn solid magenta, unvisited ones stay dashed.
Two colorways, one title block: the day chart and a red-lit night panel, following the system theme.
One continuous flight: the journey is a single route the camera travels, never a page swap.

options.label: The Almanac Sky
options.lineage: The Nautical Almanac's ephemeris tables and sky observation
options.thesis: Every place you have lived, shown under its real sky at this exact moment, computed from the sun's position.
options.viewport: The live sky over New York right now, full-bleed, with your introduction set into it; an almanac strip lists each place's local time and sun altitude.
options.risk: Closest to the window-seat skies Codex already tried, and live skies are a familiar WebGL showcase; at night several chapters go dark together.

options.label: Provenance Ribbon
options.thesis: Your career as one continuous ribbon through places and roles; established facts in solid type, reported or in-development work in hairline.
options.viewport: A tall archival sheet; the ribbon leaves New York at the top and descends through every chapter, knotting at each case.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: evidence status maps to its known/inferred type system; loses on identification, since archives are not your audience's world.
options.risk: Cream, serif and red sits near the familiar AI-portfolio look and must be pushed hard to escape it.

options.label: Oscilloscope Bench
options.thesis: Research as finding the signal in noise: each case a channel on one graticule.
options.viewport: One phosphor screen with a trace snapping out of noise behind the introduction.
options.case: Fuses for the instrumentation case only; cannot carry places or the person.
options.risk: Reads as an electronics lab, not a research practice.

options.label: Depot Destination Blind
options.thesis: Each chapter a destination course stepping under one fixed window.
options.viewport: One fixed window showing New York on a lit green cloth course.
options.case: Carries destinations, not research judgment; transit signage is not the audience's world.
options.kept: Mechanical stepping: readouts snap in whole units with one overshoot.

options.label: Sewing Pattern Envelope
options.thesis: Cases as pattern views, the visitor's chosen path traced in one red.
options.viewport: A pattern envelope front indexing the cases as views A to D.
options.case: No link to research or places.
options.kept: What you have committed to is solid; everything else stays dashed.

options.label: Football Kit Wall
options.thesis: A home and away identity with a crest that never moves.
options.viewport: A kit front with the name arched over a number.
options.case: Unrelated to the owner or the audience.
options.kept: Two colorways, one fixed identity mark.

options.label: Synthwave Horizon
options.thesis: Driving toward a horizon that keeps arriving.
options.viewport: A receding grid under a striped sun, the name extruded above.
options.case: Genre cliche with no product truth.
options.kept: One continuous forward journey, never a page swap.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean UX research portfolio executed at full craft: introduction, three featured cases, about, contact.
canonCard.viewport: Name and research focus, then featured case rows with problem, role and status.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other strong research portfolios by design; no award-level motion idea.
